points.text: When Daud killed Jalut (Goliath), it lifted the morale of Talut’s army and they won the battle over the Canaanites. Daud later inherited the kingdom from Talut.
Allah gave to him the Zaboor or Psalms. The Zaboor was not a completely new book. Some parts of the Torah had got lost, and the Zaboor came to fill in these gaps.

verses.text: They (Talut’s army) put the unbelievers to flight by the leave of Allah, and Daud (a.s) killed Jalut. Allah gave Daud the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him what Allah pleased (reference is made to the Zaboor). (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 33)
We have exalted some prophets above the others and gave Zaboor to Daud. (Surah Al-Isra : 55)

points.text: Daud (a.s) would recite Allah’s praises in a melodious voice and Allah commanded the birds and mountains to join him in glorifying Allah’s praises.

verses.text: We bestowed Our blessings on Daud and commanded: “O mountains! Join him in glorifying My praise” and a similar command was given to the birds. (Surah Saba : Verse 10)

Reminder is made of Daud (a.s), the man of strength, who was frequent in turning to Allah. We made the mountains join him in Our praises at evening and the sunrise. And the bird too, with all their flocks, join in glorifying Allah with him. (Surah S’ad : 17 to 19)

story.introduction: Allah made the iron soft for Daud and gave him wisdom and knowledge

points.text: Allah further blessed Daud (a.s) by making iron soft for him. This helped in the wars, wherein his army were better protected.

verses.text: Allah made iron soft for him, so he can make coats of armor (as instruments of war). (Surah Saba : Section 2)
We taught him (Daud) the armor’s craft, so they might protect you in your wars: yet, are you ever grateful? (Surah Al-Anbiya : 80)

points.text: Allah gave Daud (a.s) a son, Sulaiman. Allah bestowed knowledge and wisdom upon both of them.

verses.text: We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and sound judgement in speech and decision. (Surah S’ad : Verse 20)
We bestowed knowledge on Daud and Sulaiman. They both said (in gratitude): “Praise be to Allah Who has exalted us above many of His believing servants”. (Surah An-Naml: Verse 16)
Allah said: “O Family of Daud! Work gratefully. Only a few of My servants are truly grateful.” (Surah Saba : Section 2)

points.text: There are two interesting incidents captured in the Quran relating to Daud (a.s):

story.introduction: Incident of two angels who came to Daud (a.s)’s prayer chamber at night

verses.text: Mention is made of the incident when two people (who were actually angels) entered into Daud (a.s)’s prayer chamber through climbing over the wall. (Surah S’ad : Section 2)
Daud (a.s) was terrified, but they said: “Have no fear. We are two contending parties. One of us has oppressed the other. So judge between us with truth.” (Surah S’ad : Section 2)
They were 2 brothers and one of them said: “He has ninety-nine sheep, while I have only one. Still he says: ‘Turn her over to me’ and he has overcome me in argument”. (Surah S’ad : Section 2)

(Without listening to the other complainant), Daud (a.s) said “He has certainly wronged you in seeking to add your sheep to his flock: in fact, many partners are unjust to one another, except those who believe and do good deeds, and they are few indeed”. (Surah S’ad : Section 2)
Daud (a.s) (saw that the litigants had disappeared and he) realized that this was a test from Allah (and judging himself by his own standard, he considered himself guilty). (Surah S’ad : Section 2)

points.text: Daud (a.s) realized his mistakes in two counts:
One was that, he did not listen to the other party before making the judgement. The other, was that he made a judgement when he was in a state of fear and in haste.

verses.text: So he sought forgiveness of his Rabb and fell down prostrating himself and turned to Allah in repentance. (Sajdah) (Surah S’ad : Section 2)

Allah forgave his error and said to him: “O Daud! We have made you a vicegerent (i.e. ruler) in the earth. So rule among the people with justice and do not follow your own desires”. (Surah S’ad : Section 2)

story.introduction: Case of a flock of sheep that destroyed a farm owner’s land

verses.text: And remember Daud and Sulaiman, when the two were judging a case regarding the field into which the sheep of a certain people had strayed by night, and We were watching them to arrive at judgement. (Surah Al-Anbiya : 78)
At that time We gave Sulaiman insight to arrive at the right decision, although We had given judgement and knowledge to both of them (Surah Al-Anbiya : 79)

points.text: When a flock of Sheep from a certain people had strayed into the fields of another person and destroyed its crops, the matter was brought to the court of Daud (a.s). Young Sulaiman (a.s), who was only about 12 years of age was also present at the court of his father.

Daud (a.s) had ruled that the owner of the sheep should give his sheep as a compensation for the land owner’s loss. Allah gave insight to Sulaiman and he requested his father if he could speak. Daud (a.s) gave him permission to speak.

Sulaiman said that the sheep be given to the owners of the land. They will take care of the sheep and will use its milk and wool.  Meantime, the owners of the sheep will work on the land to plough and bring it back to the way that it was.  Once the field comes back to the way it was, each one will take back his original property.
This insightful decision was accepted by all at the court and Daud (a.s) loved the ruling and ordered that it be followed accordingly.
